title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers created AI-generated videos impersonating a real immigration attorney to defraud vulnerable immigrants on social media. The system was deployed without any human verification of identity, allowing hundreds of fake accounts across multiple platforms to operate freely before detection. It would have taken platform-level identity verification or manual review of accounts claiming professional credentials to catch this before thousands of people were targeted.

The failure is one of impersonation enabled by AI video synthesis. Scammers used the technology to create content falsely claiming the attorney could secure legal status for a flat fee, then directed victims to off-platform payment methods. The platforms themselves—TikTok, Facebook, Instagram—did not prevent the creation of fraudulent accounts in another person's name, though an anti-piracy company eventually removed thousands of them after the attorney discovered the scheme.

It is not established what specific AI tools were used, how the scammers obtained video or audio of the attorney, or whether the platform companies had knowledge of the fraud before removal. The financial and personal harm to victims is documented in reporting but the total scope and the investigation's outcome are not yet known.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney, Angel Leal, who has practiced law for over 30 years, says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos showing Leal offering immigration services he never provided, such as claiming to secure US residency for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office. An anti-piracy company he hired has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, forcing Leal to change his personal phone number.

The scams typically start with social media videos directing people to contact a WhatsApp number, where fraudsters send fake contracts and request payment through digital platforms like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Some videos feature fake testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal for helping them obtain legal status. Leal warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of promises requiring immediate payment. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the fraud's origins. His office does not request phone payments and advises consumers to watch for these warning signs.
